headline: Central bankers warn AI boom risks global financial crash due to 'excessive' debt-fuelled investment
summary: The Bank for International Settlements (BIS) warns that "excessive" debt-fuelled spending on AI infrastructure and opaque transactions could trigger a financial meltdown akin to the 2008 credit crunch.
details: Debt-fuelled spending on AI is increasing the risk of a global financial crisis, according to central bankers. The Bank for International Settlements (BIS) warns that "excessive" investment in AI data centers and complex transactions could lead to a meltdown similar to the 2008 credit crunch.

The BIS, often called the bank for central banks, highlighted growing "peril" from the intricate financial ties between AI giants, shadow banks, and data center developers. They cautioned that financial stability could be at risk if the AI boom experiences a bust.

Pablo Hernández de Cos, BIS general manager, questioned the wider economic benefits of the boom and warned of serious consequences if "AI exuberance" reverses. He noted the risk of over-investment as firms compete for market dominance, making the sector vulnerable if AI under-delivers.

This warning from the BIS is one of the strongest yet, echoing concerns from the Bank of England and the International Monetary Fund. Both have compared current AI valuations to the excesses seen before the 2008 crisis and the dotcom bubble.

Big tech companies like OpenAI and Nvidia are using complex financial deals, including loans from chipmakers to bot developers for chip purchases, to fund AI development. Shadow banks are also heavily investing in AI data centers to capitalize on demand.

The report notes "signs of stress" in private credit funds within the shadow banking industry, with some facing redemption requests and withdrawal blocks. This sector has grown rapidly as mainstream banking regulations tightened.

The BIS drew parallels between the current AI infrastructure surge and historical speculative bubbles, including the dotcom boom, British railway mania of the 1840s, and the "roaring 20s." These precedents highlight potential downside risks in the near term.

Recent volatility in US and Asian AI-linked stocks, alongside warnings about bottlenecks in data center construction or chip shortages, further underscore the fragility. Apple's recent price increase due to higher microchip costs also impacted global tech stocks.

headline_marked: [[Sophon PFG-1 AI ASIC features 330 GB on-die DRAM]], eliminates HBM entirely
headline: Sophon PFG-1 AI ASIC features 330 GB on-die DRAM, eliminates HBM entirely
summary: This monolithic-3D AI ASIC delivers up to 4,200 TFLOPS FP8 and 2,100 TFLOPS BF16, outperforming HBM4 GPUs in low-batch training and inference while significantly cutting hardware costs.
details: Sophon PFG-1 is a monolithic-3D (M3D) AI ASIC featuring 330 GB of on-die DRAM, eliminating the need for High-Bandwidth Memory (HBM). This 750 mm² die delivers 4,200 TFLOPS FP8 and 2,100 TFLOPS BF16, making it a unified solution for both training and inference. It achieves this performance in a compact 7.5 cm² footprint.

The architecture is built on a 28 nm Si CMOS base tier with a 32-tier 2D-TMD CMOS MAC stack. Its core innovation is the 2T0C 2D-TMD gain-cell DRAM, embedded at the BEOL Metal-3 layer of each memory tier. This allows for fully read-write memory that supports both forward/backward training passes and low-batch inference.

Sophon's design allows for an 80B-parameter BF16 training model to fit entirely on-die, with ~10 GB of activation headroom. For inference, it serves an 80B model at 7,219 tokens/s in native BF16 or 14,438 tokens/s in FP8 mode. This makes it a single part that can be elastically repartitioned between training and serving without hardware changes.

Compared to 2026 HBM4 parts like NVIDIA Rubin (R200) and AMD Instinct MI455X, Sophon delivers ~2.7–3.1x higher 80B batch-1 training throughput per die. It also achieves ~48–53x higher single-stream FP8 decode throughput. This significant advantage stems from its ~191–214x higher weight bandwidth compared to an HBM4 package, addressing a critical memory wall.

The economic implications are substantial, with Sophon eliminating the HBM memory line item that can account for 25.7% of a rack's cost in systems like NVIDIA VR200. This results in an estimated ~9.9x to 11.6x lower hardware Bill of Materials (BOM) than Rubin or MI455X. The 2T0C 2D-TMD gain-cell DRAM provides multi-second retention with extremely low off-current density.

This unique DRAM cell solves the memory wall for both inference and training workloads. For inference, it offers low read energy per bit and idle leakage, crucial for keeping models resident. For training, it provides in-place writability, low write energy, and unlimited write endurance, essential for the billions of write cycles required by large models.
